_note: Owner-directed 2026-10-19: AI ladder items 1-3 plus an AI strategy and change leadership business bundle; the five capture foundationals brought into the catalog (D only), Communication split into written and spoken, plus Collaboration and Professional responsibility. Problem solving is listed separately under proposedProgramLevel and is not inserted until its scoring approach is decided. Drafted by Claude (Opus 5.5) for owner review; not AI-pipeline output. Insert unlinked with origin = gc_authored, as with the 2026-10-12 business-acumen batch; target links and weights come with P3. Cards for the new competencies are in 2026-10-15-bundle-cards.json (the card apply needs one file covering every active competency).

newCompetencies.name: AI literacy and responsible use
newCompetencies.knowDescriptor: Knows in plain terms how generative AI produces output (patterns learned from training data, generating likely content), why it can be fluent and wrong, why the same request can give different results, and the rules for handling client and personal data in AI tools.
newCompetencies.understandDescriptor: Understands why AI output has to be checked against sources and domain knowledge before it is trusted, why convenience and confidentiality can conflict, and why disclosing AI use and keeping content provenance matter for trust in brand and print work.
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Explains what an AI tool did on a piece of work and where it could be wrong, decides what information may go into which tool, and discloses or labels AI-generated content as the applicable policy requires.
newCompetencies.rationale: The base the other AI bundles assume. Scored on K/U/D like quantitative-literacy, because understanding how the tools work is the point: it is what carries over as specific tools change. Boundary: directing a tool to a finished output stays in ai-tool-direction; setting a team's AI policy stays in quality-frameworks.

newCompetencies.name: AI strategy and change leadership
newCompetencies.knowDescriptor: Knows where AI is changing the economics of creative and print work (the cost of a version falling, value moving to judgment and systems), common adoption patterns, and the parts of a change plan: roles, training, communication and measures.
newCompetencies.understandDescriptor: Understands why cheaper production changes pricing and the service mix rather than only cutting cost, why AI adoption fails more often on people and process than on tools, and why staff and clients need to know what changes for them.
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Develops an AI direction for a team, business unit or the organization's own operations (which offerings and roles change, how pricing or the service mix responds) with a change plan covering training and measures, and presents it to decision makers.
newCompetencies.rationale: Owner-requested (2026-10-19) to cover the top of the AI ladder: leading an organization through AI, not only using or evaluating tools. Boundary: benchmarking one tool for an adopt/drop decision stays in ai-tool-evaluation; writing and operating the AI-use policy stays in quality-frameworks; making a client's ROI case stays in proposal-development.

newCompetencies.name: Agency
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently makes and owns choices in their work (direction, scope, tools, goals) and follows through without step-by-step direction.
newCompetencies.rationale: One of the five baseline foundationals already scored on D in every course capture; brought into the catalog so it has a card and can carry career demand.

newCompetencies.name: Attention to detail
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently delivers work that is correct in execution as well as concept (file specifications, type, alignment, labels, spelling) and catches their own errors before handoff.
newCompetencies.rationale: Baseline capture foundational, brought into the catalog. Boundary: operating a production inspection system stays in quality-control.

newCompetencies.name: Resilience
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently works through setbacks (failed attempts, critique, open-ended constraints) by revising and persisting rather than abandoning the work or settling.
newCompetencies.rationale: Baseline capture foundational, brought into the catalog.

newCompetencies.name: Curiosity
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently goes beyond stated requirements to find out how and why things work, seeking sources, techniques or questions the assignment did not require.
newCompetencies.rationale: Baseline capture foundational, brought into the catalog.

newCompetencies.name: Written communication
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently writes clear, organized documents suited to their reader (briefs, reports, specifications, messages) that the reader can act on without follow-up.
newCompetencies.rationale: Split from the capture foundational Communication (owner, 2026-10-19). O*NET's Writing and Written Expression items need a home on the demand side. Visual communication stays in the technical bundles; a proposal's business case stays in proposal-development.

newCompetencies.name: Spoken communication
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently presents, explains and listens well in speech (presentations, critiques, client and team conversations), adjusting to the audience and handling questions.
newCompetencies.rationale: Split from the capture foundational Communication (owner, 2026-10-19). O*NET's Speaking, Active Listening and Oral Expression items need a home on the demand side.

newCompetencies.name: Collaboration and teamwork
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently works well with others on shared work (dividing tasks, keeping commitments, integrating others' contributions, working through disagreement) so the group's result is better than any one member's.
newCompetencies.rationale: Named in the capture agent's list of foundationals to add when evidenced. Boundary: managing staff performance stays in team-coordination.

newCompetencies.name: Professional responsibility and ethics
newCompetencies.doDescriptor: Consistently acts with professional integrity: represents their own and others' work honestly (including AI's part), respects intellectual property and confidentiality, meets commitments, and owns mistakes.
newCompetencies.rationale: Named in the capture agent's list of foundationals to add when evidenced (Professionalism, Ethical Judgment). Boundary: knowing contract and licensing rules stays in contracts-ip-licensing; knowing AI data and disclosure rules stays in ai-literacy. This bundle is the conduct, not the knowledge.

descriptorRevisions.why: AI ladder item 1 (owner, 2026-10-19): task-level decisions about what to give AI and what a person must check.
descriptorRevisions.knowDescriptor: Knows the capabilities and failure modes of major generative AI tools across image, copy, and video, which kinds of tasks they handle well and which they do not, and how to script or assemble a lightweight personal AI workflow or tool (a prompt chain, a small automation) to speed their own work.
descriptorRevisions.understandDescriptor: Understands why AI outputs require iteration grounded in human judgment about what good looks like, why deciding which parts of a task to give AI and what a person must verify is part of the craft, and why building a small tool for one's own workflow is now baseline fluency for this target — distinct from building a system other people run, which is target 5's job.
descriptorRevisions.doDescriptor: Splits a task into parts for AI and parts for a person, recognizes when not to use AI, directs the AI parts from prompt through final output that meets brand quality standards while checking what a person must verify, and, where useful, builds or configures a small AI tool or automation for their own workflow and documents it well enough to reuse.

descriptorRevisions.why: AI ladder item 2 (owner, 2026-10-19): governance beyond review steps (AI-use policy, client data, disclosure and content credentials).
descriptorRevisions.knowDescriptor: Knows the dimensions on which creative, production, and AI-assisted output is evaluated — brand, legal/regulatory, and print-quality standards — where each kind of check belongs in a workflow, and what an AI-use policy covers: which data may enter which tools, how AI-generated content is disclosed or labeled (including content credentials), and who signs off.
descriptorRevisions.understandDescriptor: Understands why quality and compliance checking requires domain expertise and can't be fully automated, why someone must stay accountable for AI-assisted output specifically, and why an AI-use policy has to be specific enough to apply on a real job.
descriptorRevisions.doDescriptor: Builds or operates a quality/compliance review step in a real workflow — a brand check, a legal/regulatory check, or a print-quality check — that catches failure modes consistently, including checks on AI-assisted output, and writes or applies an AI-use policy for a team or job covering data, disclosure and sign-off.

proposedProgramLevel.name: Problem solving in the discipline
proposedProgramLevel.status: PROPOSED — not inserted until the owner decides how it is measured
proposedProgramLevel.doDescriptor: Solves unfamiliar production, design and business problems in the discipline by bringing organized domain knowledge to bear: diagnosing, attempting, learning from failed attempts and revising, across varied conditions.
proposedProgramLevel.derivedFrom: Not scored per course. Derived at program level from (a) the productive-failure and structured-reflection conditions course capture already records, (b) depth 4+ on Do (adapts to new conditions) across the technical bundles, and (c) the Phase 1B scaffolding analysis of how those conditions recur across the sequence.
proposedProgramLevel.rationale: Problem solving is not a transferable generic skill (Background; problem-solving deep dive): it is well-organized domain knowledge deployed under demanding conditions. A per-course score would credit any assignment called a problem. A catalog entry still matters: O*NET's Complex Problem Solving and Critical Thinking items need a home on the demand side, and the program view should show it explicitly.
